row.evidence: Hive's SCIM guide says "You must have an existing Hive workspace with the Enterprise Security Add-on", which the pricing page sells as the "SSO, enterprise security & control" flexible add-on at +$5 each per user on Teams (included on Enterprise).
row.notes: New row. Pricing page (yearly view, 'save 33%'): Free $0 (up to 10 members), Starter $5, Teams $12 per user/mo, Enterprise Contact Sales ('Flexible add-ons included'). SCIM and SAML need the Enterprise Security add-on, sold in the Teams calculator as 'SSO, enterprise security & control' at +$5 per user per month (the calculator adds each add-on to the per-user price), so the SCIM price is $12 + $5 = $17/user/mo on yearly billing; whether Starter can buy the add-on is not stated. One help article (custom SAML) still says a Hive Enterprise plan is required (see conflicts). Hive documents a public SCIM 2.0 API (https://scim.hive.com/v2/{workspaceId}, bearer = Hive API key of a system admin) for Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, JumpCloud and Ping; Google Workspace only via third-party SCIM bridges. Okta OIN app is SCIM (create, update, deactivate, group push); Entra gallery app is SSO + JIT only. SCIM DELETE or active=false removes the user from the workspace (account kept, re-provisionable). REST API v2 (same API key or OAuth2) lists, invites, updates and removes members and manages teams; 1000 requests/min per user; the plan that includes it is not stated (pricing lists 'Enterprise API' on Enterprise).

auth.token_source: My Settings (Edit profile) > API Info > Generate API Key; the key owner must be a system admin; same key as the REST API

deprovision.data_retained: SCIM DELETE or active=false removes the user from the workspace but keeps the Hive account; the user goes to the removed-users list and can be re-provisioned. Hive's manual-removal article says direct messages with the user are deleted and projects private to the user are deleted; assigned actions and comments remain.

custom.how: Okta mappings beyond userName, givenName, familyName and email are ignored and not persisted.

limitations.text: Only the eq filter operator is supported.
PATCH /Users only supports replace on active and externalId (password is a no-op); name and email updates need PUT and apply only to active members.
Okta app maps only userName (must be an email), first name, last name and email; passwords are not synced.
Creating a group whose displayName already exists updates that group; all group members must be active workspace members.
Google Workspace is supported only via third-party SCIM bridges.

scim.notes: ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas and ResourceTypes endpoints are not listed in the SCIM reference. The Okta guide assumes SAML SSO is set up, but does not say SCIM fails without it.

endpoints.purpose: List users who share a workspace with the caller
Update a user profile (org admins can update users)
Invite a workspace member by email
Remove a workspace member (userId in body)
Rename a team or replace its members
Assign a user role tag (resourcing label, not a permission role)

webhooks_user_events.notes: POST /webhooks exists but the reference does not enumerate trigger values, so user-event triggers are unconfirmed.

rate_limits.text: 1000 requests per minute per user; 429 beyond that.

limitations.text: Every endpoint acts with the permissions of the API key or token owner.

okta.notes: OIN app capabilities checked: SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push, Group Linking.

entra.notes: Gallery tutorial covers SAML SSO and JIT; no Entra provisioning tutorial (hive-provisioning-tutorial 404). Hive's SCIM reference names Azure AD (Entra ID) as compatible with the generic endpoint.

google.notes: Custom SAML app in Google Workspace; SCIM only via third-party bridges.

onelogin.notes: Hive's security article cites a 'Hive' SAML 2.0 app in the OneLogin store; OneLogin catalogue page not checked (blocks bots). SCIM reference lists OneLogin as compatible.

jumpcloud.notes: SCIM reference lists JumpCloud as compatible with the generic endpoint; jumpcloud.com/support returned 403.

conflicts.text: Most Hive help articles and the pricing calculator make SAML/SCIM an Enterprise Security add-on (+$5/user/mo, available on Teams); the custom SAML article says you must 'Have a Hive Enterprise plan' and the GSuite article says 'Hive Enterprise accounts support SAML SSO'.

open_questions: Can the Enterprise Security add-on be bought on Starter, or only on Teams?
Does SCIM removal free the paid seat, and does it end active sessions?
Which plans include the REST API ('Enterprise API' is listed only on Enterprise)?
Is there an audit-log API, and which webhook triggers exist?
SCIM API token expiry is not documented.
